abstract: We show that at sufficiently large inverse-temperature $\beta>0$, the 3D Ising model on the torus, under boundary conditions that have a positive slope $\theta_1,\theta_2>0$, has a GFF scaling limit for its interface. The proof goes through three steps of a Tetris map, which lets cubes drop according to gravity in each of the three axes, yielding Solid-On-Solid (SOS), Half-Monotone SOS (HMSOS) and monotone surfaces (dimers). We establish GFF limits sequentially, in particular resolving the analogous problem for the $(2+1)$D SOS. A crucial ingredient is an improved RG analysis for interacting dimers, which is of independent interest: it relaxes the assumptions on interactions from being uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$ to only being typically small.
hook: The rough surface between phases in a 3D Ising model at low temperature is Gaussian-free-field random.
summary: For a 3D Ising model on a torus with tilted boundary conditions at large inverse temperature, the interface converges to a Gaussian free field. The proof steps through three gravity-style maps down to dimer surfaces, and resolves the analogous 2+1D solid-on-solid case. It holds only for low temperature and sloped boundaries.
title: GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris
